plain_english: When the concept can impress the self by itself, independent of other means — fallen from bonded activity, by the grace of pure knowledge, having attained the form of the Lord's power, relied on as the means, it brings forth śākta knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: tatra yadā vikalpaḥ svayam eva saṃskāram ātmani upāyāntaranirapekṣatayaiva kartuṃ prabhavati tadā asau pāśavavyāpārāt pracyutaḥ śuddhavidyānugraheṇa parameśaśaktirūpatām āpanna upāyatayā avalambyamānaḥ śāktaṃ jñānam āvirbhāvayati

plain_english: This is settled in the very next ahnika.
sanskrit_cite: tad etac ca nirṇītam anantara eva āhnike

plain_english: But when the concept depends on another means for its own impression — taking mind, breath, body, pots and the rest, limited in form, as means, reaching subtlety — it brings forth āṇava knowledge. Therein the mind is meditation-natured; the breath, gross and subtle — the first, articulation-natured; articulation, moreover, means the five functions beginning with breath; the subtle is denoted by letter-sound, to be said later; the body, arrangement-specific in nature, is denoted by instrument-sound; pots and the rest are external, to be praised as means by pit-pot-liṅga-worship and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: yadā tu upāyāntaram asau svasaṃskārārthaṃ vikalpo 'pekṣate tadā buddhiprāṇadehaghaṭādikān parimitarūpān upāyatvena gṛhṇan aṇutvaṃ prāpta āṇavaṃ jñānam āvirbhāvayati tatra buddhiḥ dhyānātmikā prāṇaḥ sthūlaḥ sūkṣmaś ca ādya uccāraṇātmā uccāraṇaṃ ca nāma pañca prāṇādyā vṛttayaḥ sūkṣmas tu varṇaśabdavācyo vakṣyate dehaḥ saṃniveśaviśeṣātmā karaṇaśabdavācyaḥ ghaṭādayo bāhyāḥ kumbhasthaṇḍilaliṅgapūjādyupāyatayā kīrtayiṣyamāṇāḥ

plain_english: Here the fitting meditation is to be taught: that self-luminous supreme tattva, contained in all tattvas — having meditated it in the knowledge of one's own heart, let him meditate there the union of knower, instrument and known, the triad of fire, sun and moon, until he becomes the great Bhairava-fire, fanned by the wind of meditation. From that wheel, wrapped in the twelve old power-flames, having emerged through some pore-door, let him contemplate it resting outside in the graspable self; and by that one at rest, let him meditate how the external is first filled by moon-form in the order of creation, then lit by sun-form in preservation, then dissolved by the fire-form of dissolution, then made unsurpassable-selfhood.
sanskrit_cite: tatra dhyānaṃ tāvat iha ucitam upadekṣyāmaḥ yat etat svaprakāśaṃ sarvatattvāntarbhūtaṃ paraṃ tattvam uktaṃ tad eva nijahṛdayabodhe dhyātvā tatra pramātṛpramāṇaprameyarūpasya vahnyarkasomatritayasya saṃghaṭṭaṃ dhyāyet yāvat asau mahābhairavāgniḥ dhyānavātasamiddhākāraḥ sampadyate tasya prāktanaśaktijvālādvādaśakaparivṛtasya cakrātmanaḥ cakṣurādīnām anyatamasuṣiradvāreṇa niḥsṛtasya bāhye grāhyātmani viśrāntaṃ cintayet tena ca viśrāntena prathamaṃ tadbāhyaṃ somarūpatayā sṛṣṭikrameṇa prapūritaṃ tataḥ arkarūpatayā sthityā avabhāsitaṃ tato 'pi saṃhāravahnirūpatayā vilāpitaṃ tataḥ anuttarātmatām āpāditaṃ dhyāyet

plain_english: Thus that wheel becomes complete with all divisions of external things.
Then with that wheel let him meditate the residual habit-states, made thus.
sanskrit_cite: tato vāsanāśeṣān api bhāvān tena cakreṇa itthaṃ kṛtān dhyāyet

plain_english: For this unceasing meditator, who determines from his own consciousness the real series of creation, preservation and dissolution — consciousness-merely-real — and the supremacy of creation's autonomy, at once comes the Bhairava-state.
sanskrit_cite: evam asya anavarataṃ dhyāyinaḥ svasaṃvinmātraparamārthān sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhāraprabandhān sṛṣṭyādisvātantryaparamārthatvaṃ ca svasaṃvido niścinvataḥ sadya eva bhairavībhāvaḥ

plain_english: By practice, all desired attainments and the rest as well.
The self-luminous all-self-tattva, the triad beginning with measure.
Having entered within, standing, let him meditate in the abode of heart-bliss.
That twelve-great-power-ray-wheel-Lord, all-pervading.
Emerging by ethers outside, let him meditate it bearing the states beginning with creation.
That mandala swallowing all outer and inner being — in the self.
Resting, let the yogin contemplate — thus is the spread of the self.
sanskrit_cite: viśrāmyan bhāvayed yogī syād evam ātmanaḥ prathā

plain_english: These are the summary-verses.
Thus meditation.

When about to articulate the breath: first he rests in the emptiness of the heart; then outside, from the arising of breath; then also toward the external, by the moon-filling of apāna, seeing all-selfness; then he becomes desiring no other; then from the arising of samāna he experiences union-rest; then from the arising of the udāna-fire he grasps the construction of measure and measured.
sanskrit_cite: tatra prāṇam uccicārayiṣuḥ pūrvaṃ hṛdaya eva śūnye viśrāmyati tato bāhye prāṇodayāt tato 'pi bāhyaṃ prati apānacandrāpūraṇena sarvātmatāṃ paśyati tataḥ anyanirākāṅkṣo bhavati tataḥ samānodayāt saṃghaṭṭaviśrāntim anubhavati tata udānavahnyudaye mātṛmeyādikalanāṃ grasate

plain_english: In the pacification of its swallowing-fire, at the arising of vyāna, devoid of every limitation, it flashes.

Thus from emptiness up to vyāna: these rests — own-bliss, blisslessness, supreme-bliss, brahman-bliss, great-bliss, consciousness-bliss — six bliss-levels are taught; of which one is the connector, without arising or setting, inner-rest-truth-natured: world-bliss.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ śūnyāt prabhṛti vyānāntaṃ yā etā viśrāntayaḥ tā eva nijānando nirānandaḥ parānando brahmānando mahānandaḥ cidānanda iti ṣaṭ ānandabhūmaya upadiṣṭāḥ yāsām ekaḥ anusaṃdhātā udayāstamayavihīnaḥ antarviśrāntiparamārtharūpo jagadānandaḥ

plain_english: Therefore in these articulation-levels, resting each separately two-wise or wholly, he makes the rest-tattva attainable, distinct from that body, breath and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: tat etāsu uccārabhūmiṣu pratyekaṃ dvyādiśaḥ sarvaśo vā viśrāmya anyat taddehaprāṇādivyatiriktaṃ viśrāntitattvam āsādayati

plain_english: Keeping in mind that very secret of the articulation of the creation-dissolution seed, let him impress the concept; and in these rests, each separately, five states become, from the depth of entry.
sanskrit_cite: tad eva sṛṣṭisaṃhārabījoccāraṇarahasyam anusaṃdadhat vikalpaṃ saṃskuryāt āsu ca viśrāntiṣu pratyekaṃ pañca avasthā bhavanti praveśatāratamyāt

plain_english: Therein first bliss, from contact with the portion of fullness; then arising, a moment, in the embodimentlessness of the habitual; then tremor, from self-power overpowering, loosening body-identity; then sleep, from the dissolution of outwardness.
sanskrit_cite: tatra prāg ānandaḥ pūrṇatāṃśasparśāt tata udbhavaḥ kṣaṇaṃ niḥśarīratāyāṃ rūḍheḥ tataḥ kampaḥ svabalākrāntau dehatādātmyaśaithilyāt tato nidrā bahirmukhatvavilayāt

plain_english: Thus, the non-self-being dissolved into self-being: from the all-pervasiveness of the self, the non-self-being dissolves in the self — therefore whirling, from the arising of great pervasion.
sanskrit_cite: ittham anātmani ātmabhāve līne svātmanaḥ sarvamayatvāt ātmani anātmabhāvo vilīyate iti ato ghūrṇiḥ mahāvyāptyudayāt

plain_english: These are the levels beginning with waking, up to the limit beyond the fourth.
And these levels occur in the entry of the triangle-root-heart-pace-upward-kuṇḍalinī-wheel.
Thus in articulation-rest: what is supreme pulsation, the knowable dissolved into rest; what is dawning knowable; what is already-dawned knowable — that triad of marks we will say at the proper time.
sanskrit_cite: evam uccāraviśrāntau yat paraṃ spandanaṃ galitāśeṣavedyaṃ yac ca unmiṣad vedyaṃ yac ca unmiṣitavedyaṃ tad eva liṅgatrayam iti vakṣyāmaḥ svāvasare

plain_english: And the supreme mark here is the yogini-heart.
Therein the primary pulsation-form, by contraction-and-expansion nature, arising as pair-form, from gaining the rest of the visarga-portion — enough.
sanskrit_cite: tatra mukhyā spandanarūpatā saṃkocavikāsātmatayā yāmalarūpatodayena visargakalāviśrāntilābhāt ity alam

plain_english: Non-luminous: here entry.
First in self-knowing, then resting in the knowable, let him complete the knowable.
sanskrit_cite: pūrvaṃ svabodhe tadanu prameye viśramya meyaṃ paripūrayeta

plain_english: In the complete, here he rests — the distinction of measurer and measured; quickly let him withdraw.
sanskrit_cite: pūrṇe 'tra viśrāmyati mātṛmeyavibhāgam āśv eva sa saṃhareta

plain_english: Having pervaded, then he rests; those would be, together with emptiness, the six means-levels.
sanskrit_cite: vyāptyātha viśrāmyati tā imāḥ syuḥ śūnyena sākaṃ ṣaḍupāyabhūmyaḥ

plain_english: Breath and the rest are not-after-vyāna; and dissolved in it, the manifestation beginning with waking.
sanskrit_cite: prāṇādayo vyānanapaścimās tallīnaś ca jāgrat prabhṛti prapañcaḥ

plain_english: Established in practice here, in the abode of creation-dissolution contemplation, let him grow before long.
These are the inner-verses.
Thus articulation.

In this articulation flashes a sound, a letter, almost an imitation of the unmanifest; its primary form is in the creation-dissolution seed — from its practice comes the gain of supreme-consciousness. For instance: in kā, at the end of mā, in sācke, in anacke, or articulated within, remembered — the touch of consciousness-pulsation, equally distinguished, complete because it disregards convention; even for those who regard convention, words producing its meaning like a mirage and the rest; from the touch of unsurpassable consciousness, let him unify the heart-throat-lips, the pair of twelve-ends and the heart — the letter-secret.
sanskrit_cite: asmin eva uccāre sphuran avyaktānukṛtiprāyo dhvaniḥ varṇaḥ tasya sṛṣṭisaṃhārabīje mukhyaṃ rūpaṃ tadabhyāsāt parasaṃvittilābhaḥ tathāhi kādau mānte sācke anacke vā antaruccārite smṛte vā samaviśiṣṭaḥ saṃvitspandasparśaḥ samayānapekṣitvāt paripūrṇaḥ samayopekṣiṇo 'pi śabdāḥ tadarthabhāvakā manorājyādivat anuttarasaṃvitsparśāt ekīkṛtahṛtkaṇṭhoṣṭho dvādaśāntadvayaṃ hṛdayaṃ ca ekīkuryāt iti varṇarahasyam

plain_english: The white-yellow-and-rest inner letter, born immediately after the contemplation of inner touch, being manifested, causes consciousness to be experienced — so some say.
sanskrit_cite: antaḥsparśadvimarśānantarasamudbhūtaṃ sitapītādyāntaraṃ varṇam udbhāvyamānaṃ saṃvidam anubhāvayati iti kecit

plain_english: By the absence of the expressible, from consciousness-pulsation, by the two checks of moon-and-sun motion.
Of which, by equal entry, complete in the form of the consciousness-seed-mass letter.
This is the inner-verse.
Thus the letter-rule.
The operation of mudrā-revelation we will say.
